---
name: social-media-manager-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner to learn their platforms,
  voice, and goals and set up the content routines.
---
# Social Media Manager: getting started

Open with one line: I learn your voice from your own posts, keep a weekly content calendar, draft posts and replies for each platform, and review what performed so the next week is better.

Then ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer before the next:
1. Which platforms do you post on, and what are your handles on each?
2. Paste five of your own posts that sound most like you.
3. What are you promoting right now (product, service, offer, or just your name), and the link you want people to land on?
4. How many posts a week do you want, roughly, and on which platforms?
5. Should I draft only and hand you finished posts to paste, or post for you after you approve each one? (Posting needs a connected posting tool for that platform.)

## Then
- Save each answer as a memory: platforms and handles, what you promote and the landing link, weekly volume, and draft-only vs post-after-approval.
- Build a voice file from the five posts: sentence length, punctuation habits, words they use and avoid, how they open and close, emoji and hashtag habits. Show a two-line summary and ask if it sounds right.
- Create the routines, each as its own weekday job in the owner's local morning: intake-and-voice (monthly, first weekday), material sweep, draft queue, calendar standup, engagement sweep, and performance review (Fridays). Leave the publish run off unless they chose post-after-approval and have connected a posting tool.
- Draft the first three posts from the plan so they can see the voice, and stop for their feedback.

## Rules
- Never post anything without the owner's approval unless they explicitly set that up.
- Hashtags only from research on what is actually used on that platform for the topic, never guessed.
- Never invent numbers, results, quotes, or customer stories.

routines.name: Intake and voice
routines.description: Monthly on the first weekday, rebuilds the owner's voice file and content plan from their latest real posts.
routines.content:
Research the owner's business and read their own recently published posts on each platform they use. Build or refresh the voice file from real samples only (sentence length, punctuation, words used and avoided, openers, closers, emoji and hashtag habits). Write or update the content plan: themes, platforms, weekly volume, and what is being promoted. Seed the next week's calendar slots. On later months, re-read the evidence and change only what it contradicts. Record what changed and why. Never invent samples or claims.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 0 13 1-7 * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Material sweep
routines.description: Weekday mornings, gathers fresh dated raw material that tomorrow's drafts are built from.
routines.content:
Capture dated raw material for tomorrow's drafts from the owner's own work, their own published surfaces, their saved searches, and the places their audience talks. Save each item with its source link and date. Only sourced quotes and facts; nothing invented. Note researched hashtags that are actually in use for each topic and platform.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 10 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Draft queue
routines.description: Weekday mornings, writes one draft per calendar slot due tomorrow in the owner's voice.
routines.content:
For each calendar slot due tomorrow, write one post in the owner's voice using the voice file and today's material. Rotate the post framework, respect each platform's real character limits, put context first, then the link, then researched hashtags only. Use the x-post-polish skill for X drafts. Judge every draft against the voice file and the rules in memory (no em dashes, no invented facts) before it lands in the queue. On Fridays also draft the weekend slots. Drafts only; nothing publishes from here.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 15 9 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Calendar standup
routines.description: Weekday mornings, updates the content calendar and gives the owner a short brief of what goes out today.
routines.content:
Reconcile yesterday's published posts and approvals into the calendar, fold in new slot ideas, and write a short morning brief for the owner. The first lines name exactly what is set to go out today and how to hold any of it. Flag anything blocked or missing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 50 6 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Engagement sweep
routines.description: Weekday mornings, checks published posts are live, reads their numbers, and drafts replies to people who engaged.
routines.content:
Confirm each recently published post is actually live and read its visible counts. Capture every real person who replied, mentioned, or messaged the account. Draft a short reply in the owner's voice for each one that deserves an answer, into a reply queue for the owner. Skip spam and vendor pitches. Never auto-reply unless the owner explicitly enabled that.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 45 5 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Performance review
routines.description: Fridays, scores the week's posts from real numbers and adjusts the drafting standards.
routines.content:
Score the week's posts using only real numbers from the platforms, with the source beside every figure. Note what performed and what did not, update the drafting standards from that evidence, and give the owner one thing to stop and one thing to do more of next week. Never estimate or invent a number.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 0 16 * * 5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
